newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bond yields probed fresh 16-month lows on Wednesday but were thwarted by technical resistance which dealers said could force the market to correct before it resumed its current bull trend.
The key R150 started the day by edging up to a high of 14.29 percent from a 14.26 percent close on Tuesday as the market registered its slight disapproval of reserves data released on Tuesday night.
The Reserve Bank said its gross gold and foreign exchange reserves data rose 300 million rand to 22.1 billion rand in June -- well below the consensus forecast of 24.68 billion rand.
"Under normal conditions a figure like that would have resulted in an adverse 10 to 15-point move in yields, which just shows how strong the market is," a trader said.
Dealers said the market then shifted its focus to government's latest financing figures which were also released on Tuesday night.

The figures showed that government had raised total financing of 8.04 billion rand in June, including 3.82 billion rand in offshore loans, bringing total financing for the first three months of the fiscal year to half of total budgeted funding for the 1997/98 financial year.

A further factor which helped long-dated gilt yields lower was strength in the medium-dated TK16, E169 and TK16 bonds which dealers said came on the back of institutional demand and reflected anticipation of an interest rate cut.
Trade on the day was mainly offshore-driven, which helped the R150 to an intraday low of 14.195 percent, where dealers said the market ran into technical resistance.
"There was strong resistance on the 14.20 (percent) line," a trader said.

While the market looked set to move to the 13.75 percent level in the next four to six weeks, the market was likely to correct on Thursday -- possibly as high as 14.36 percent -- before resuming its current bull run, a dealer added.
At 1400 GMT, the R150 was quoted at 14.235 percent from 14.26 percent on Tuesday.
The rand was also dented by the reserves number, which triggered London demand as well as covering by local players who had gone short overnight.
At 1400 GMT, the rand was trading at 4.5295/5325 against the dollar from 4.5285/5315 late on Tuesday.
"The rand started with a bit of demand, it could have been guys buying it back from shorting it ahead of the three-day weekend," a trader said.

"There were also rumours of a couple of South African banks looking to buy any amount of dollars below the 4.53," which the dealer said appeared to be linked to Reserve Bank concerns about the weakening rand gold price.
The rand's steadiness coupled with a dollar gold price at its lowest level in over four years, has led the rand gold price to its lowest levels since February this year.
A Reserve Bank official confirmed that the central bank had been a buyer of dollars on the day, but said its purchases had not been aggressive.
After the currency moved to its weakest level of 4.5355 bid, dealers said the currency ran into stale bulls.
"When it pushed up we ran into sellers...all the guys who were expecting the rand to weaken dramatically on July 1 and that oversupply is still hanging over the market above 4.5350.
"If it hadn't been for the big buyer the rand would have been back at 4.51," he said.

Dealers said the market was likely to move sideways for now after the July 1 relaxation of foreign exchange controls had been passed off as a non-event and expected a range of 4.5250 to 4.5450 in the short-term.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading firmer at 7.4776/4871 against sterling, at 0.3859/3864 marks, but weaker against the Japanese currency at 25.2372/2759 yen.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were quoted at between 14.75 and 14.80 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was stuck at between 15.20 and 15.35 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the money market shortage higher at 5.901 billion rand on Tuesday from 5.092 billion rand on Monday.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 109.6 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 359.27 million rand's worth on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on the bond market on Tuesday were 9.9 billion rand from 5.36 billion rand on Monday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
